member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.DynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod
member.summary: Chooses the Dynamic Global Illumination method. Not compatible with Forward Shading.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.IndirectLightingColor
member.summary: Adjusts indirect lighting color. (1,1,1) is default. (0,0,0) to disable GI. The show flag 'Global Illumination' must be enabled to use this property.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.IndirectLightingIntensity
member.summary: Scales the indirect lighting contribution. A value of 0 disables GI. Default is 1. The show flag 'Global Illumination' must be enabled to use this property.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.RayLightingMode
member.summary: Controls how Lumen rays are lit when Lumen is using Hardware Ray Tracing. By default, Lumen uses the Surface Cache for best performance, but can be set to 'Hit Lighting' for higher quality.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.LumenSceneLightingQuality
member.summary: Scales Lumen Scene's quality. Larger scales cause Lumen Scene to be calculated with a higher fidelity, which can be visible in reflections, but increase GPU cost.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.LumenSceneDetail
member.summary: Controls the size of instances that can be represented in Lumen Scene. Larger values will ensure small objects are represented, but increase GPU cost.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.LumenSceneViewDistance
member.summary: Sets the maximum view distance of the scene that Lumen maintains for ray tracing against. Larger values will increase the effective range of sky shadowing and Global Illumination, but increase GPU cost.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.LumenSceneLightingUpdateSpeed
member.summary: Controls how much Lumen Scene is allowed to cache lighting results to improve performance. Larger scales cause lighting changes to propagate faster, but increase GPU cost.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.FinalGatherQuality
member.summary: Scales Lumen's Final Gather quality. Larger scales reduce noise, but greatly increase GPU cost.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.FinalGatherLightingUpdateSpeed
member.summary: Controls how much Lumen Final Gather is allowed to cache lighting results to improve performance. Larger scales cause lighting changes to propagate faster, but increase GPU cost and noise.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.LumenFinalGatherScreenTraces
member.summary: Whether to use screen space traces for Lumen Global Illumination. Screen space traces bypass Lumen Scene and instead sample Scene Depth and Scene Color. This improves quality, as it bypasses Lumen Scene, but causes view dependent lighting.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.MaxTraceDistance
member.summary: Controls the maximum distance that Lumen should trace while solving lighting. Values that are too small will cause lighting to leak into large caves, while values that are large will increase GPU cost.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.DiffuseColorBoost
member.summary: Allows brightening indirect lighting by calculating material diffuse color for indirect lighting. Values above 1 (original diffuse color) aren't physically correct, but they can be useful as an art direction knob to increase the amount of bounced light in the scene. Best to keep below 2 as it also causes reflections to be brighter than the scene.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.SkylightLeaking
member.summary: Controls what fraction of the skylight intensity should be allowed to leak. This can be useful as an art direction knob (non-physically based) to keep indoor areas from going fully black.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.SkylightLeakingTint
member.summary: Color tint for Lumen Skylight Leaking.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.FullSkylightLeakingDistance
member.summary: Controls the distance from a receiving surface where skylight leaking reaches its full intensity. Smaller values make the skylight leaking flatter, while larger values create an Ambient Occlusion effect.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.SceneCaptureCacheResolutionScale
member.summary: Scale factor for Lumen Surface Cache resolution, for Scene Capture. Smaller values save GPU memory, at a cost in quality. Defaults to 0.5 if not overridden.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.LumenReflectionQuality
member.summary: Scales the Reflection quality. Larger scales reduce noise in reflections, but increase GPU cost.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.HighQualityTranslucencyReflections
member.summary: Whether to use high quality mirror reflections on the front layer of translucent surfaces. Other layers will use the lower quality Radiance Cache method that can only produce glossy reflections. Increases GPU cost when enabled.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.MaxRoughnessToTrace
member.summary: Sets the maximum roughness value for which Lumen still traces dedicated reflection rays. Higher values improve reflection quality, but greatly increase GPU cost.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.MaxReflectionBounces
member.summary: Sets the maximum number of recursive reflection bounces. 1 means a single reflection ray (no secondary reflections in mirrors). Currently only supported by Hardware Ray Tracing with Hit Lighting.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.MaxRefractionBounces
member.summary: The maximum count of refraction event to trace. When hit lighting is used, Translucent meshes will be traced when LumenMaxRefractionBounces > 0, making the reflection tracing more expenssive.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.ScreenSpaceReflectionMaxRoughness
member.summary: Until what roughness we fade the screen space reflections, 0.8 works well, smaller can run faster

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.MegaLights
member.summary: Allows forcing MegaLights on or off for this volume, regardless of the project setting for MegaLights. MegaLights will stochastically sample lights, which allows many shadow casting lights to be rendered efficiently, with a consistent and low GPU cost. When MegaLights is enabled, other direct lighting algorithms like Deferred Shading will no longer be used, and other shadowing methods like Ray Traced Shadows, Distance Field Shadows and Shadow Maps will no longer be used. MegaLights requires Hardware Ray Tracing and Shader Model 6.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.CubemapTexture
member.summary: The Ambient cubemap (Affects diffuse and specular shading), blends additively which if different from all other settings here

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.CameraShutterSpeed
member.summary: The camera shutter in 1/seconds.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.ISO
member.summary: The camera sensor sensitivity

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.DepthOfFieldFstop
member.summary: Defines the opening of the camera lens, Aperture is 1/fstop, typical lens go down to f/1.2 (large opening), larger numbers reduce the DOF effect

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.DepthOfFieldMinFstop
member.summary: Defines the maximum opening of the camera lens to control the curvature of blades of the diaphragm. Set it to 0 to get straight blades.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.Numberofdiaphragmblades
member.summary: Defines the number of blades of the diaphragm within the lens (between 4 and 16).

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.ExposureCompensation
member.summary: Logarithmic adjustment for the exposure. Only used if a tonemapper is specified. 0: no adjustment, -1:2x darker, -2:4x darker, 1:2x brighter, 2:4x brighter, ...

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.AutoExposureBiasBackup
member.summary: With the auto exposure changes, we are changing the AutoExposureBias inside the serialization code. We are storing that value before conversion here as a backup. Hopefully it will not be needed, and removed in the next engine revision.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.Override_AutoExposureBiasBackup
member.summary: With the auto exposure changes, we are also changing the auto exposure override value, so we are storing that backup as well.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.ApplyPhysicalCameraExposure
member.summary: Only affects Manual exposure mode.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.ExposureCompensationCurve
member.summary: Exposure compensation based on the scene EV100. Used to calibrate the final exposure differently depending on the average scene luminance. 0: no adjustment, -1:2x darker, -2:4x darker, 1:2x brighter, 2:4x brighter, ...

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.ExposureMeteringMask
member.summary: Exposure metering mask. Bright spots on the mask will have high influence on auto-exposure metering and dark spots will have low influence.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.MinBrightness
member.summary: Auto-Exposure minimum adaptation. Eye Adaptation is disabled if Min = Max. Auto-exposure is implemented by choosing an exposure value for which the average luminance generates a pixel brightness equal to the Constant Calibration value. The Min/Max are expressed in pixel luminance (cd/m2) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings).

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.MaxBrightness
member.summary: Auto-Exposure maximum adaptation. Eye Adaptation is disabled if Min = Max. Auto-exposure is implemented by choosing an exposure value for which the average luminance generates a pixel brightness equal to the Constant Calibration value. The Min/Max are expressed in pixel luminance (cd/m2) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings).

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.SpeedUp
member.summary: In F-stops per second, should be >0

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.SpeedDown
member.summary: In F-stops per second, should be >0

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.HistogramLogMin
member.summary: Histogram Min value. Expressed in Log2(Luminance) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings)

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.HistogramLogMax
member.summary: Histogram Max value. Expressed in Log2(Luminance) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings)

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.AutoExposureCalibrationConstant_DEPRECATED
member.summary: Calibration constant for 18% albedo, deprecating this value.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.HighlightContrast
member.summary: Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer. Contrast of the base layer is reduced based on this value. Value less than 1 will enable local exposure. Good values are usually in the range 0.6 .. 1.0.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.ShadowContrast
member.summary: Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer. Contrast of the base layer is reduced based on this value. Value less than 1 will enable local exposure. Good values are usually in the range 0.6 .. 1.0.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.HighlightContrastCurve
member.summary: Local Exposure Highlight Contrast based on the scene EV100. Used to calibrate Local Exposure differently depending on the average scene luminance.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.ShadowContrastCurve
member.summary: Local Exposure Shadow Contrast based on the scene EV100. Used to calibrate Local Exposure differently depending on the average scene luminance.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.HighlightThreshold
member.summary: Threshold used to determine which regions of the screen are considered highlights.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.ShadowThreshold
member.summary: Threshold used to determine which regions of the screen are considered shadows.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.DetailStrength
member.summary: Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer. Value different than 1 will enable local exposure. This value should be set to 1 in most cases.

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.BlurredLuminanceBlend
member.summary: Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer. Blend between bilateral filtered and blurred luminance as the base layer. Blurred luminance helps preserve image appearance and specular highlights, and reduce ringing. Good values are usually in the range 0.4 .. 0.6

member.name: F:UnrealSharp.Engine.FPostProcessSettings.BlurredLuminanceKernelSizePercent

member.summary: Defines the target FPS for motion blur. Makes motion blur independent of actual frame rate and relative to the specified target FPS instead. A value of zero makes the motion blur dependent on the actual frame rate.

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimaryDataAsset
member.summary:
A DataAsset that implements GetPrimaryAssetId and has asset bundle support, which allows it to be manually loaded/unloaded from the AssetManager. Instances of native subclasses can be created directly as Data Assets in the editor and will use the name of the native class as the PrimaryAssetType. Or, blueprint subclasses can be created to add variables and then subclassed again by Data Only Blueprints that set those variables. With blueprint subclasses, use Data Only Blueprints (and not Data Asset instances) to properly handle data inheritance and updating the parent class.
The PrimaryAssetType will be equal to the name of the first native class going up the hierarchy, or the highest level blueprint class. IE, if you have UPrimaryDataAsset -> UParentNativeClass -> UChildNativeClass -> DataOnlyBlueprintClass the type will be ChildNativeClass. Whereas if you have UPrimaryDataAsset -> ParentBlueprintClass -> DataOnlyBlueprintClass the type will be ParentBlueprintClass. To change this behavior, override GetPrimaryAssetId in your native class or copy those functions into a different native base class.

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent
member.summary: PrimitiveComponents are SceneComponents that contain or generate some sort of geometry, generally to be rendered or used as collision data. There are several subclasses for the various types of geometry, but the most common by far are the ShapeComponents (Capsule, Sphere, Box), StaticMeshComponent, and SkeletalMeshComponent. ShapeComponents generate geometry that is used for collision detection but are not rendered, while StaticMeshComponents and SkeletalMeshComponents contain pre-built geometry that is rendered, but can also be used for collision detection.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.AlwaysCreatePhysicsState
member.summary: Indicates if we'd like to create physics state all the time (for collision and simulation). If you set this to false, it still will create physics state if collision or simulation activated. This can help performance if you'd like to avoid overhead of creating physics state when triggers

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.MultiBodyOverlap
member.summary: If true, this component will generate individual overlaps for each overlapping physics body if it is a multi-body component. When false, this component will generate only one overlap, regardless of how many physics bodies it has and how many of them are overlapping another component/body. This flag has no influence on single body components.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.DynamicShadow
member.summary: Controls whether the primitive should cast shadows in the case of non precomputed shadowing. This flag is only used if CastShadow is true and if FirstPersonPrimitiveType is not set to FirstPerson.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.StaticShadow
member.summary: Whether the object should cast a static shadow from shadow casting lights. This flag is only used if CastShadow is true and if FirstPersonPrimitiveType is not set to FirstPerson.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.VolumetricTranslucentShadow
member.summary: Whether the object should cast a volumetric translucent shadow. Volumetric translucent shadows are useful for primitives with smoothly changing opacity like particles representing a volume, but have artifacts when used on highly opaque surfaces. This flag is only used if CastShadow is true and if FirstPersonPrimitiveType is not set to FirstPerson.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.SelfShadowOnly
member.summary: When enabled, the component will only cast a shadow on itself and not other components in the world. This is especially useful for first person weapons, and forces bCastInsetShadow to be enabled.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.FarShadow

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.ShadowTwoSided

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.ReceiveCSMShadows

It means that all collision geometries of the asset are merged vertically resulting in a grid of vertical columns that encompass the asset. This can be useful to represent the interior of the surface and prevent navmesh inside.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.CanCharacterStepUpOn
member.summary: Determine whether a Character can step up onto this component. This controls whether they can try to step up on it when they bump in to it, not whether they can walk on it after landing on it. See: FWalkableSlopeOverride

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.LightingChannels
member.summary: Channels that this component should be in. Lights with matching channels will affect the component. These channels only apply to opaque materials, direct lighting, and dynamic lighting and shadowing. Lighting channels are only supported on translucent materials using forward shading (i.e. when not using the translucency lighting volume).

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.RayTracingGroupCullingPriority
member.summary: Defines how quickly it should be culled. For example buildings should have a low priority, but small dressing should have a high priority.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.ExcludefromHLODLevels
member.summary: Which specific HLOD levels this component should be excluded from

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.RayTracingGroupId
member.summary: Defines run-time groups of components. For example allows to assemble multiple parts of a building at runtime. -1 means that component doesn't belong to any group.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.VisibilityId
member.summary: Used for precomputed visibility

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.CustomPrimitiveDataDefaults
member.summary: Optional user defined default values for the custom primitive data of this primitive

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.CustomPrimitiveDataInternal
member.summary: Custom data that can be read by a material through a material parameter expression. Set data using SetCustomPrimitiveData* functions

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.TranslucencySortPriority
member.summary:
Translucent objects with a lower sort priority draw behind objects with a higher priority. Translucent objects with the same priority are rendered from back-to-front based on their bounds origin. This setting is also used to sort objects being drawn into a runtime virtual texture.
Ignored if the object is not translucent. The default priority is zero. Warning: This should never be set to a non-default value unless you know what you are doing, as it will prevent the renderer from sorting correctly. It is especially problematic on dynamic gameplay effects.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.DrawinVirtualTextures
member.summary: Array of runtime virtual textures into which we draw the mesh for this actor. The material also needs to be set up to output to a virtual texture.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.VirtualTextureLODBias
member.summary: Bias to the LOD selected for rendering to runtime virtual textures.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.VirtualTextureSkipMips
member.summary: Number of lower mips in the runtime virtual texture to skip for rendering this primitive. Larger values reduce the effective draw distance in the runtime virtual texture. This culling method doesn't take into account primitive size or virtual texture size.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.VirtualTextureMinCoverage
member.summary: Set the minimum pixel coverage before culling from the runtime virtual texture. Larger values reduce the effective draw distance in the runtime virtual texture.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.DrawinMainPass
member.summary: Controls if this component draws in the main pass as well as in the virtual texture.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.BodyInstance

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.OnComponentBeginOverlap
member.summary: Event called when something starts to overlaps this component, for example a player walking into a trigger. For events when objects have a blocking collision, for example a player hitting a wall, see 'Hit' events.

member.summary: If true, this component will be visible in ray tracing effects. Turning this off will remove it from ray traced reflections, shadows, etc.

member.summary: If true, this component will be rendered in the main pass (z prepass, basepass, transparency)

member.summary: If true, this component will be rendered in the depth pass even if it's not rendered in the main pass

member.summary: Whether the primitive receives decals.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.Holdout
member.summary: If this is True, this primitive will render black with an alpha of 0, but all secondary effects (shadows, reflections, indirect lighting) remain. This feature requires activating the project setting(s) "Alpha Output", and "Support Primitive Alpha Holdout" if using the deferred renderer.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.OwnerNoSee
member.summary: If this is True, this component won't be visible when the view actor is the component's owner, directly or indirectly. Will be internally set to true when FirstPersonPrimitiveType is set to WorldSpaceRepresentation.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.OnlyOwnerSee
member.summary: If this is True, this component will only be visible when the view actor is the component's owner, directly or indirectly.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.CastShadow
member.summary: Controls whether the primitive component should cast a shadow or not.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.EmissiveLightSource
member.summary: Whether the primitive will be used as an emissive light source.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.AffectDynamicIndirectLighting
member.summary: Controls whether the primitive should influence indirect lighting.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.AffectIndirectLightingWhileHidden
member.summary: Controls whether the primitive should affect indirect lighting when hidden. This flag is only used if bAffectDynamicIndirectLighting is true.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.AffectDistanceFieldLighting
member.summary: Controls whether the primitive should affect dynamic distance field lighting methods. This flag is only used if CastShadow is true.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.ContactShadow
member.summary: Whether the object should cast contact shadows. This flag is only used if CastShadow is true.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.DynamicInsetShadow
member.summary: Whether this component should create a per-object shadow that gives higher effective shadow resolution. Useful for cinematic character shadowing. Assumed to be enabled if bSelfShadowOnly is enabled.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.HiddenShadow
member.summary: If true, the primitive will cast shadows even if bHidden is true. Controls whether the primitive should cast shadows when hidden. This flag is only used if CastShadow is true and if FirstPersonPrimitiveType is not set to WorldSpaceRepresentation.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.LightAttachmentsAsGroup
member.summary: Whether to light this component and any attachments as a group. This only has effect on the root component of an attachment tree. When enabled, attached component shadowing settings like bCastInsetShadow, bCastVolumetricTranslucentShadow, etc, will be ignored. This is useful for improving performance when multiple movable components are attached together.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.ExcludeFromLightAttachmentGroup
member.summary: If set, then it overrides any bLightAttachmentsAsGroup set in a parent.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.SingleSampleShadowFromStationaryLights
member.summary: Whether the whole component should be shadowed as one from stationary lights, which makes shadow receiving much cheaper. When enabled shadowing data comes from the volume lighting samples precomputed by Lightmass, which are very sparse. This is currently only used on stationary directional lights.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.RenderCustomDepthPass
member.summary: If true, this component will be rendered in the CustomDepth pass (usually used for outlines)

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.VisibleInSceneCaptureOnly
member.summary: When true, will only be visible in Scene Capture

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.HiddenInSceneCapture
member.summary: When true, will not be captured by Scene Capture

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.FirstPersonPrimitiveType
member.summary: If this is set to FirstPerson, the camera FirstPersonFieldOfView and FirstPersonScale parameters will be used on this component. These parameters can be used to render the component with a different field of view and a smaller depth range such that clipping with the scene can be avoided. This is useful for rendering first person view geometry.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.StaticWhenNotMoveable
member.summary: When false, the underlying physics body will contain all sim data (mass, inertia tensor, etc) even if mobility is not set to Moveable

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.CustomDepthStencilWriteMask
member.summary: Mask used for stencil buffer writes.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.CustomDepthStencilValue
member.summary: Optionally write this 0-255 value to the stencil buffer in CustomDepth pass (Requires project setting or r.CustomDepth == 3)

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.TranslucencySortDistanceOffset
member.summary:
Modified sort distance offset for translucent objects in world units. A positive number will move the sort distance further and a negative number will move the distance closer.
Ignored if the object is not translucent. Warning: Adjusting this value will prevent the renderer from correctly sorting based on distance. Only modify this value if you are certain it will not cause visual artifacts.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.BoundsScale
member.summary: Scales the bounds of the object. This is useful when using World Position Offset to animate the vertices of the object outside of its bounds. Warning: Increasing the bounds of an object will reduce performance and shadow quality! Currently only used by StaticMeshComponent and SkeletalMeshComponent.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.MoveIgnoreActors
member.summary: Set of actors to ignore during component sweeps in MoveComponent(). All components owned by these actors will be ignored when this component moves or updates overlaps. Components on the other Actor may also need to be told to do the same when they move. Does not affect movement of this component when simulating physics. See: IgnoreActorWhenMoving()

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.MoveIgnoreComponents
member.summary: Set of components to ignore during component sweeps in MoveComponent(). These components will be ignored when this component moves or updates overlaps. The other components may also need to be told to do the same when they move. Does not affect movement of this component when simulating physics. See: IgnoreComponentWhenMoving()

member.name: M:UnrealSharp.Engine.UPrimitiveComponent.GetMaxDepenetrationVelocity(UnrealSharp.Core.FName)
member.summary: The maximum velocity used to depenetrate this object from others when spawned or teleported with initial overlaps (does not affect overlaps as a result of normal movement). A value of zero will allow objects that are spawned overlapping to go to sleep without moving rather than pop out of each other. E.g., use zero if you spawn dynamic rocks partially embedded in the ground and want them to be interactive but not pop out of the ground when touched. A negative value means that the config setting CollisionInitialOverlapDepenetrationVelocity will be used.

member.name: T:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent
member.summary:
ProjectileMovementComponent updates the position of another component during its tick.
Behavior such as bouncing after impacts and homing toward a target are supported.
Normally the root component of the owning actor is moved, however another component may be selected (see SetUpdatedComponent()). If the updated component is simulating physics, only the initial launch parameters (when initial velocity is non-zero) will affect the projectile, and the physics sim will take over from there.
See: UMovementComponent

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.InitialSpeed
member.summary: Initial speed of projectile. If greater than zero, this will override the initial Velocity value and instead treat Velocity as a direction.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.MaxSpeed
member.summary: Limit on speed of projectile (0 means no limit).

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.RotationFollowsVelocity
member.summary: If true, this projectile will have its rotation updated each frame to match the direction of its velocity.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.RotationRemainsVertical
member.summary: If true, this projectile will have its rotation updated each frame to maintain the rotations Yaw only. (bRotationFollowsVelocity is required to be true)

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.ShouldBounce
member.summary: If true, simple bounces will be simulated. Set this to false to stop simulating on contact.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.InitialVelocityInLocalSpace
member.summary: If true, the initial Velocity is interpreted as being in local space upon startup. See: SetVelocityInLocalSpace()

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.ForceSubStepping
member.summary: If true, forces sub-stepping to break up movement into discrete smaller steps to improve accuracy of the trajectory. Objects that move in a straight line typically do *not* need to set this, as movement always uses continuous collision detection (sweeps) so collision is not missed. Sub-stepping is automatically enabled when under the effects of gravity or when homing towards a target. See: MaxSimulationTimeStep, MaxSimulationIterations

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.SimulationEnabled
member.summary: If true, does normal simulation ticking and update. If false, simulation is halted, but component will still tick (allowing interpolation to run).

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.SweepCollision
member.summary: If true, movement uses swept collision checks. If false, collision effectively teleports to the destination. Note that when this is disabled, movement will never generate blocking collision hits (though overlaps will be updated).

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.IsHomingProjectile
member.summary: If true, we will accelerate toward our homing target. HomingTargetComponent must be set after the projectile is spawned. See: HomingTargetComponent, HomingAccelerationMagnitude

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.BounceAngleAffectsFriction
member.summary: Controls the effects of friction on velocity parallel to the impact surface when bouncing. If true, friction will be modified based on the angle of impact, making friction higher for perpendicular impacts and lower for glancing impacts. If false, a bounce will retain a proportion of tangential velocity equal to (1.0 - Friction), acting as a "horizontal restitution".

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.IsSliding
member.summary: If true, projectile is sliding / rolling along a surface.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.InterpMovement
member.summary: If true and there is an interpolated component set, location (and optionally rotation) interpolation is enabled which allows the interpolated object to smooth uneven updates of the UpdatedComponent's location (usually to smooth network updates). This requires using SetInterpolatedComponent() to indicate the visual component that lags behind the collision, and using MoveInterpolationTarget() when the new target location/rotation is received (usually on a net update). See: SetInterpolatedComponent(), MoveInterpolationTarget()

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.InterpRotation
member.summary: If true and there is an interpolated component set, rotation interpolation is enabled which allows the interpolated object to smooth uneven updates of the UpdatedComponent's rotation (usually to smooth network updates). Rotation interpolation is *only* applied if bInterpMovement is also enabled. See: SetInterpolatedComponent(), MoveInterpolationTarget()

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.ThrottleInterpolation
member.summary: If true, throttle interpolation when not relevant. See: ThrottleInterpolationSkipFramesNotRecent, ThrottleInterpolationSkipFramesRecent, ThrottleInterpolationThresholdNotRenderedShortTime, ThrottleInterpolationThresholdNotRenderedLongTime

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.SimulationUseScopedMovement
member.summary: If true, uses FScopedMovementUpdate to avoid moving the UpdatedComponent more than once during a tick during simulation. This also defers overlap updates and some impact events until after the simulation update completes, so it may delay important events and continue deflection, so use with caution.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.InterpolationUseScopedMovement
member.summary: If true, uses FScopedMovementUpdate to avoid moving the attached interpolated object's children more than once during a tick when it would both interpolate and move during projectile simulation. This also defers overlap updates for the interpolated object until after the simulation update completes.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.PreviousHitTime
member.summary: Saved HitResult Time (0 to 1) from previous simulation step. Equal to 1.0 when there was no impact.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.PreviousHitNormal
member.summary: Saved HitResult Normal from previous simulation step that resulted in an impact. If PreviousHitTime is 1.0, then the hit was not in the last step.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.ProjectileGravityScale
member.summary: Custom gravity scale for this projectile. Set to 0 for no gravity.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.Buoyancy
member.summary: Buoyancy of UpdatedComponent in fluid. 0.0=sinks as fast as in air, 1.0=neutral buoyancy

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.Bounciness
member.summary: Percentage of velocity maintained after the bounce in the direction of the normal of impact (coefficient of restitution). 1.0 = no velocity lost, 0.0 = no bounce. Ignored if bShouldBounce is false.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.Friction
member.summary: Coefficient of friction, affecting the resistance to sliding along a surface. Normal range is [0,1] : 0.0 = no friction, 1.0+ = very high friction. Also affects the percentage of velocity maintained after the bounce in the direction tangent to the normal of impact. Ignored if bShouldBounce is false. See: bBounceAngleAffectsFriction

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.BounceVelocityStopSimulatingThreshold
member.summary: If velocity is below this threshold after a bounce, stops simulating and triggers the OnProjectileStop event. Ignored if bShouldBounce is false, in which case the projectile stops simulating on the first impact. See: StopSimulating(), OnProjectileStop

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.MinFrictionFraction
member.summary: When bounce angle affects friction, apply at least this fraction of normal friction. Helps consistently slow objects sliding or rolling along surfaces or in valleys when the usual friction amount would take a very long time to settle.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.OnProjectileBounce
member.summary: Called when projectile impacts something and bounces are enabled.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.OnProjectileStop
member.summary: Called when projectile has come to a stop (velocity is below simulation threshold, bounces are disabled, or it is forcibly stopped).

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.HomingAccelerationMagnitude
member.summary: The magnitude of our acceleration towards the homing target. Overall velocity magnitude will still be limited by MaxSpeed.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.HomingTargetComponent
member.summary: The current target we are homing towards. Can only be set at runtime (when projectile is spawned or updating). See: bIsHomingProjectile

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.MaxSimulationTimeStep
member.summary:
Max time delta for each discrete simulation step. Lowering this value can address precision issues with fast-moving objects or complex collision scenarios, at the cost of performance.
WARNING: if (MaxSimulationTimeStep * MaxSimulationIterations) is too low for the min framerate, the last simulation step may exceed MaxSimulationTimeStep to complete the simulation. See: MaxSimulationIterations, bForceSubStepping

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.MaxSimulationIterations
member.summary:
Max number of iterations used for each discrete simulation step. Increasing this value can address precision issues with fast-moving objects or complex collision scenarios, at the cost of performance.
WARNING: if (MaxSimulationTimeStep * MaxSimulationIterations) is too low for the min framerate, the last simulation step may exceed MaxSimulationTimeStep to complete the simulation. See: MaxSimulationTimeStep, bForceSubStepping

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.BounceAdditionalIterations
member.summary: On the first few bounces (up to this amount), allow extra iterations over MaxSimulationIterations if necessary.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.InterpLocationTime
member.summary: "Time" over which most of the location interpolation occurs, when the UpdatedComponent (target) moves ahead of the interpolated component. Since the implementation uses exponential lagged smoothing, this is a rough time value and experimentation should inform a final result. A value of zero is effectively instantaneous interpolation.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.InterpRotationTime
member.summary: "Time" over which most of the rotation interpolation occurs, when the UpdatedComponent (target) moves ahead of the interpolated component. Since the implementation uses exponential lagged smoothing, this is a rough time value and experimentation should inform a final result. A value of zero is effectively instantaneous interpolation.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.InterpLocationMaxLagDistance
member.summary: Max distance behind UpdatedComponent which the interpolated component is allowed to lag.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.InterpLocationSnapToTargetDistance
member.summary: Max distance behind UpdatedComponent beyond which the interpolated component is snapped to the target location instead. For instance if the target teleports this far beyond the interpolated component, the interpolation is snapped to match the target.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.ThrottleInterpolationThresholdNotRenderedShortTime
member.summary: Time after not rendered recently when we consider throttling interpolation.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.ThrottleInterpolationThresholdNotRenderedLongTime
member.summary: Time after not rendered for a long time when we consider throttling interpolation.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.ThrottleInterpolationSkipFramesRecent
member.summary: When recently relevant, skip this many frames of interpolation if throttling is enabled.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.ThrottleInterpolationSkipFramesNotRecent
member.summary: When not recently relevant, skip this many frames of interpolation if throttling is enabled.

member.name: M:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.IsVelocityUnderSimulationThreshold
member.summary: Returns true if velocity magnitude is less than BounceVelocityStopSimulatingThreshold.

member.name: M:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.StopSimulating(UnrealSharp.Engine.FHitResult)
member.summary: Clears the reference to UpdatedComponent, fires stop event (OnProjectileStop), and stops ticking (if bAutoUpdateTickRegistration is true).

member.name: M:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.MoveInterpolationTarget(UnrealSharp.CoreUObject.FVector,UnrealSharp.CoreUObject.FRotator)
member.summary: Moves the UpdatedComponent, which is also the interpolation target for the interpolated component. If there is not interpolated component, this simply moves UpdatedComponent. Use this typically from PostNetReceiveLocationAndRotation() or similar from an Actor.

member.name: M:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.ResetInterpolation
member.summary: Resets interpolation so that interpolated component snaps back to the initial location/rotation without any additional offsets.

member.name: M:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.IsInterpolationComplete
member.summary: Returns whether interpolation is complete because the target has been reached. True when interpolation is disabled.

member.name: M:UnrealSharp.Engine.UProjectileMovementComponent.LimitVelocity(UnrealSharp.CoreUObject.FVector)
member.summary: Don't allow velocity magnitude to exceed MaxSpeed, if MaxSpeed is non-zero.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MobileShading
member.summary: The shading path to use on mobile platforms. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor. Forward shading will force MSAA. Mobile HDR is required for Deferred Shading.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MobileAntiAliasing
member.summary: The mobile default anti-aliasing method.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.FloatPrecisionMode
member.summary: Project wide mobile float precision mode for shaders and materials. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.AllowDitheredLODTransition
member.summary: Whether to support 'Dithered LOD Transition' material option on mobile platforms. Enabling this may degrade performance as rendering will not benefit from Early-Z optimization.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.EnablevirtualtexturesupportonMobile
member.summary: Whether to support virtual textures on mobile. Requires general virtual texturing option enabled as well. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.GameDiscardsUnusedMaterialQualityLevels
member.summary: When running in game mode, whether to keep shaders for all quality levels in memory or only those needed for the current quality level. Unchecked: Keep all quality levels in memory allowing a runtime quality level change. (default) Checked: Discard unused quality levels when loading content for the game, saving some memory.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.OcclusionCulling
member.summary: Allows occluded meshes to be culled and not rendered.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MinScreenRadiusforLights
member.summary: Screen radius at which lights are culled. Larger values can improve performance but causes lights to pop off when they affect a small area of the screen.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.MinScreenRadiusforEarlyZPass
member.summary: Screen radius at which objects are culled for the early Z pass. Larger values can improve performance but very large values can degrade performance if large occluders are not rendered.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Warnaboutnoprecomputedvisibility
member.summary: Displays a warning when no precomputed visibility data is available for the current camera location. This can be helpful if you are making a game that relies on precomputed visibility, e.g. a first person mobile game.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.TextureStreaming
member.summary: When enabled textures will stream in based on what is visible on screen.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.UseDXT5NormalMaps
member.summary: Whether to use DXT5 for normal maps, otherwise BC5 will be used, which is not supported on all hardware. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Enablevirtualtexturesupport
member.summary: When enabled, textures can be streamed using the virtual texture system. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Enablevirtualtexturelightmaps
member.summary: When enabled, lightmaps will be streamed using the virtual texture system. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Tilesize
member.summary: Size in pixels for virtual texture tiles, will be rounded to next power-of-2. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Tilebordersize
member.summary: Size in pixels for virtual texture tile borders, will be rounded to next multiple-of-2. Larger borders allow higher degree of anisotropic filtering, but uses more disk/cache memory. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Enablevirtualtextureanisotropicfiltering
member.summary: When enabled, virtual textures will use anisotropic filtering. This adds a cost to all shaders using virtual textures. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Enablevirtualtextureontextureimport
member.summary: Enable virtual texture streaming for imported textures based on the 'Auto Virtual Texturing Size' in the texture import settings.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.EnableVirtualTextureOpacityMask
member.summary: When virtual textures contribute to opacity mask it can sometimes lead to low resolution shadow edges.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Enablevirtualtexturemeshpainting
member.summary: When enabled, mesh paint virtual textures are supported. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Meshpainttilesize
member.summary: Size in pixels for mesh paint virtual texture tiles. Will be rounded to next power-of-2. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Meshpainttilebordersize
member.summary: Size in pixels for virtual texture tile borders. Will be rounded next to multiple-of-2. Changing this setting requires restarting the editor.

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Meshpaintusecompressedtextures

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Meshpaintdefaultstaticmeshsupport

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Meshpainttexelspervertex

member.name: P:UnrealSharp.Engine.URendererSettings.Meshpaintmaximumtexturesize
